title: Amazon is shutting down Mechanical Turk on September 30 after 21 years
subtitle: The crowdsourced-labor marketplace Jeff Bezos once called "artificial artificial intelligence" closes as Scale AI, Mercor, and Prolific absorb the data-labeling market.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Amazon confirmed this week that it will shut down Mechanical Turk on September 30, 2026, and will retire SageMaker Ground Truth alongside it. The platform launched in 2005 and at peak served more than 500,000 workers taking on Human Intelligence Tasks — small data-labeling, transcription, and survey jobs that businesses paid pennies per unit to have completed. Amazon stopped taking new customers in July, which many long-time workers read as a wind-down signal.

What killed Mechanical Turk was not a single competitor but two forces arriving together. Modern models now handle the low-end tasks — image tagging, sentiment classification, short transcription — that made up most of the marketplace's volume, so the bottom of the demand curve simply disappeared. What remains at the top of the market — high-quality reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedback data, expert domain labeling, adversarial red-teaming — moved to specialist labeling firms like Scale AI, Mercor, and Prolific, which pay more per task and vet workers before onboarding.

There is a symmetry worth noting. Bezos's original pitch for MTurk in 2005 was "artificial artificial intelligence": human workers doing what computers could not, hidden behind an API. Two decades later, the API is real AI, and the human workers who trained it are being routed to the labs still building the next generation. The marketplace that made pretend-AI a viable product category is being retired by the actual product category.

For learners: MTurk's arc is a compressed version of every AI displacement story. First a job is a job, then it becomes an API, then it becomes the ground truth for a model that replaces the API. If your current work is the kind of task an API already sells cheaply, the question is not whether it will be automated. It is which layer of the stack you want to be on when it is.
